title: Technical Buyer Brief: Threat Model, Cost Advantage & Pilot Kit
author: Janelle Kim
content:
Overview

Purpose: A concise, seller-facing brief engineered for technical buyers (CTO, Head of Platform, SRE/Infra, ML Engineering, Security) that: 1) explains Redwood Inference's operational threat model and mitigations, 2) highlights unit-cost and latency advantages in typical production scenarios, and 3) provides a ready-to-run pilot kit and trial conversion pricing guidance.

TL;DR for sellers

- Risk-focused opening: emphasize data locality, KMS/HSM options, and audit logging as first-line answers to security and compliance needs.
- Economics pitch: show per-request unit economics (tokens/s) under three realistic workload profiles and a simple path to cost parity with self-hosting in 4–8 weeks for most mid-enterprise customers.
- Pilot play: secure trial (VPC or dedicated sandbox), 14–28 day target, production-simulated workload, clear success metrics (latency P50/P95, error-rate, cost-per-1000-reqs).

Audience-specific positioning

- CTO / VP Engineering:
  - Focus: long-term operational risk, vendor lock-in, SLAs, predictable spend.
  - Talking points: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, version pinning and canary rollouts, enterprise SLAs (uptime, latency objectives), and contractual data residency clauses.

- Platform / Infra Lead:
  - Focus: integration complexity, autoscaling, capacity planning.
  - Talking points: GPU pool autoscaling, burst capacity options, Terraform modules for Private, and inbound/outbound network rules for VPC mode.

- ML Engineering / Model Ops:
  - Focus: model quality, quantization, and experiment reproducibility.
  - Talking points: curated model catalog, quantization profiles per workload, KV/prefix caching, and integrated rollout and evaluation hooks.

- Security / Compliance Officer:
  - Focus: data protection, auditability, and certs.
  - Talking points: KMS/HSM integrations, per-request audit logs, SOC2/ISO/PCI readiness status, and optional on-prem air-gapped deployment.

Competitive landscape brief (one-pager style)

- Public cloud managed endpoints (e.g., Cloud A, Cloud B):
  - Strengths: integrated cloud services, single-bill.
  - Redwood counter: superior inference runtime optimizations (attention kernels, continuous batching), consistent API across private and hosted modes, built-in fallbacks and routing policies to control unit economics.

- LLM API providers (ModelAPI X, Y):
  - Strengths: fast access to new models.
  - Redwood counter: production-grade observability, dedicated/reserved capacity and deterministic pricing for heavy production workloads.

- Inference infra vendors / open-source stacks:
  - Strengths: full control, no vendor TCO.
  - Redwood counter: lower total operational burden, recommended quantization profiles, and predictable latency SLOs with SLAs for Dedicated.

Quick battlecard: objections & responses

- "We can self-host cheaper."
  1. Ask for current OPEX/CAPEX: GPU types, utilization, ops headcount.
  2. Show Redwood Optimize baseline: typical savings from batching + KV caching (15–40% token cost reduction) and decreased ops (on-call/maintenance).
  3. Offer pilot TCO template and conversion analysis.

- "How do we keep data inside our VPC?"
  1. Explain Private deployment model: control plane in-customer VPC, optional on-prem package, and KMS/HSM key separation.
  2. Point to audit log schema and retention options.

- "What about latency for interactive apps?"
  1. Share runtime P50/P95 targets by instance class (see next section) and continuous batching knobs.
  2. Recommend Dedicated GPU pools + small sequence-length optimized kernels for sub-100ms P50 in common cases.

Production performance profiles (sample SLOs for proposal)

| Profile name | Typical request | P50 latency target | P95 latency target | Unit notes |
|--------------|-----------------|--------------------:|--------------------:|-----------|
| Conversational-Small | 64 tokens prompt + 64 gen | 80 ms | 220 ms | optimized kernels, KV cache effective |
| Assist-LongContext | 1k token prompt + 512 gen | 220 ms | 650 ms | larger attention, batching tradeoffs |
| Embedding-Batch | 512 items (short texts) | 45 ms / item | 120 ms / item | batching efficiency matters |

Pilot kit: 14–28 day technical trial checklist

1. Pre-trial (sales engineer):
   - Establish scope: single API route(s) and representative prompt set.
   - Determine deployment mode: hosted sandbox vs Dedicated eval vs Private trial.
   - Define success metrics: target P95 latency, error rate < 1%, cost per 10k requests goal.

2. Provisioning (infra/SE):
   - Hosted sandbox: allocate dedicated tenant, enable logging and SSO.
   - Dedicated eval: provision GPU pool (NVIDIA A10 / A100 recommended), attach monitoring.
   - Private: deliver Terraform plan and network diagram; schedule on-prem packaging if requested.

3. Run trial (customer + SE):
   - Import prompt set and synthetic traffic generator.
   - Enable KV/prefix caching and record change in token consumption.
   - Run 48-hour production-simulated spike (2x expected QPS) and capture metrics.

4. Post-trial (sales + SE):
   - Deliver trial summary: latency distribution, cost model, security attestation, and recommended next-step (contract template attached).

Technical runbook snippets (CLI examples)

- Create sandbox route (hosted API):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SE_TOKEN>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"name":"pilot-convo","model":"redwood/gptx-1.3b","deployment":"sandbox","caching":{"prefix_kv":true}}'

- Sample Terraform snippet for Private deployment (conceptual):

provider "redwood" {
  region = "us-west-2"
  profile = "customer-prod"
}

resource "redwood_cluster" "private_eval" {
  gpu_type = "a10"
  nodes = 4
  network_mode = "vpc"
}

Pricing guidance and conversion scenarios

- Pilot pricing (recommended structure to remove friction):
  - Hosted sandbox: free for 14 days up to X tokens (negotiable by ARR), audit logs included.
  - Dedicated eval: discounted reserved short-term (monthly pro rata) for evaluation scale.
  - Private proof-of-concept: professional services + one-time packaging fee.

- Conversion scenarios: three PSA templates are recommended in commercial materials. Show simple table to stakeholders:

| Scenario | Typical monthly tokens | Recommended product | Expected billing model | Notes |
|----------|------------------------:|---------------------|------------------------|-------|
| Early-stage product | 10M–50M | Hosted API + Optimize | Pay-as-you-go + Optimize credits | Fastest time-to-value |
| Scale-up SaaS | 50M–1B | Dedicated + Optimize | Monthly reserved + overage | Predictable throughput |
| Regulated Enterprise | 200M+ with residency | Private + Dedicated hybrid | Platform fee + committed capacity | Compliance & control |

- Example discount play: 12-month commit = 20% off unit rates + Professional Services credits for Private onboarding.

Sample pitch-deck outline (3–7 slide focused version for technical buyers)

1. Problem statement: inference economics & reliability at scale
2. How Redwood solves it: runtime + orchestration + unified API
3. Performance & cost snapshots: sample SLOs and cost model summary
4. Security & compliance posture: VPC, KMS, audit logs, certs
5. Pilot proposal: timeline, resources, success criteria
6. Commercial pathway: pricing scenarios and timeline to production

Customer case study (short, anonymized)

- Customer: Global Payments Platform (anonymized)
- Use case: real-time fraud scoring + conversational routing
- Deployment: Dedicated GPU pools in us-west, private Kafka integration for event enrichment
- Outcome (90 days): 2.6x throughput improvement over prior endpoints, 28% reduction in per-transaction inference cost after caching and batching, and P95 latency improved from 820ms to 230ms.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for sales)

Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: Data residency options available per-region; Hosted retains data per tenant with configurable retention; Private keeps all data in-customer network.

Q: How are encryption keys managed?
A: Integrates with customer KMS/HSM (Bring Your Own Key) for both at-rest and envelope encryption.

Q: Can you provide audit logs for regulatory audits?
A: Yes — requestable audit log exports with configurable retention (30/90/365 days) and schema that includes per-request metadata, route, model version, and user tokens (if enabled).

Q: What certifications do you hold?
A: SOC 2 Type II (in progress for new Private workflows), ISO 27001 mapping underway — provide current attestation packet on request.

Q: How do you limit model data leakage or prompt exposure?
A: Token redaction controls, per-route data isolation, and TTL-based KV cache invalidation. We also support model validation sandboxes and safety filters for sensitive content.

Appendix: Success metric templates (copyable)

- Latency objective: P95 <= target_ms for production traffic (target_ms defined per profile).
- Cost objective: cost_per_10k_requests <= $X (negotiated in contract).
- Reliability objective: error-rate <= 0.5% sustained over 24 hours.
